content:
We need propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step1: sulfonamide formation (amine + sulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthesis: break sulfonamide to give sulfonyl chloride and aniline.

Target has sulfonamide linking two aromatic rings: aniline (para-methyl phenyl) attached to sulfonyl group attached to second phenyl bearing the α,β-unsaturated amide side chain.

Thus retrosynthetic disconnections:

1) Disconnection of sulfonamide: produce sulfonyl chloride (Ar-SO2-Cl) and aniline (Ar-NH2). The sulfonyl chloride would be derived from second phenyl sulfonyl chloride (Ar2-SO2-Cl). The aniline is the first phenyl with methyl and NH2 (para-methyl aniline). So step1: sulfonamide formation.

2) The second phenyl (Ar2) currently has a side chain: /C=C/C(=O)N-Ph-NH2 (anilide). This side chain could be formed via amide coupling (carboxylic acid to amine) after Doebner modification to create α,β-unsaturated acid then amidation.

Thus retrosynthesis: break amide bond between carbonyl and aniline (c3ccccc3N). So step2: amide formation from carboxylic acid (α,β-unsaturated acid) and aniline (aniline). So we get α,β-unsaturated acid attached to phenyl (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid can be formed via Doebner modification from aldehyde and malonic acid.

Thus step3: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde (para-methyl phenyl? Actually the aldehyde is on the second phenyl: c2ccc(CHO)cc2? The side chain is attached at para position of second phenyl. So we need aldehyde on that phenyl, then react with malonic acid to give α,β-unsaturated acid.

Thus overall three steps:

Target -> (1) sulfonamide cleavage -> sulfonyl chloride (Ar2-SO2-Cl) + aniline (Ar1-NH2). The sulfonyl chloride still has the side chain (α,β-unsaturated amide). Wait the side chain is attached to the same phenyl as sulfonyl chloride, so after cleavage we have sulfonyl chloride with side chain still attached (Ar2-SO2-Cl with side chain). That's okay.

(2) Break amide: gives α,β-unsaturated acid (Ar2-CH=CH-COOH) and aniline (c3ccccc3N). The acid still attached to sulfonyl chloride? Actually the sulfonyl chloride is attached to same phenyl, so after step2 we have sulfonyl chloride attached to phenyl bearing the unsaturated acid. So we need a template that breaks amide while preserving sulfonyl chloride.

(3) Break α,β-unsaturated acid to aldehyde + malonic acid (Doebner). So we get aldehyde (Ar2-CHO) and malonic acid (HOOC-CH2-COOH). The aldehyde is the phenyl with aldehyde.

Thus we need to find templates for each disconnection.

We can search for templates for sulfonamide formation (reverse direction). Use search with functional_groups_broken: ["sulfonamides"] maybe. Let's try.
